newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania sees wheat harvest delayed by floods, rain.
newsitem.headline: Romania sees wheat harvest delayed by floods, rain.

text.p: Romania's harvesting of what officials say is a bumper wheat crop will be seriously delayed by floods and rainfall, a top agriculture ministry official said on Monday.

"We will have big delays with the wheat harvest, especially in eastern areas where there has been heavy rain over the past three days," Agriculture Ministry Secretary of State Aurel Pana said by telephone.
Chronic problems in Romania's post-communist farm sector, like poor equipment, could further delay operations, he said.

Pana declined to give any estimate on what crop damage had been sustained. Officials have denied suggestions that adverse weather which has affected eastern European countries could have an impact on the wheat crop.
The ministry has forecast a wheat harvest of 7.07 million tonnes, almost double last year's while exports are seen at over two million tonnes.

Government statistics say 1,000 hectares of farmland are under water after 17 rivers throughout Romania spilled their banks at the weekend. One man drowned and thousands of residents were evacuated to higher ground.
Rainy weather is forecast for the next few days and could well push the completion of the harvest back further.

Romania has already taken in 50 percent of its 2.38 million hectares under wheat. Harvesting was due to be complete in the south -- the main wheat area -- by the end of July. --Diana Voicu, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
